palette.primary_role: Dark backgrounds for hero sections and footers — Peerspace uses #121212 (near-black) for nav/hero/CTA sections and #341a4a (deep purple) for accent bands; Eventbrite uses #1e0a3c for dark headings. The Knot uses pure #000 for nav and CTA buttons.
palette.accent_role: Peerspace uses #8559ec (soft purple) for links and interactive elements. The Knot uses #ff44cb (hot pink) as primary brand color for signup/search CTAs and brand accents. Eventbrite uses #3659e3 (blue) for links. Venue sites lean warm/pink/purple for emotional appeal.
palette.surface_role: White (#ffffff) as default card and content bg. Peerspace uses warm cream (#f9f1e1) for content sections and light gray (#f5f7f9). Eventbrite uses 18 distinct warm background colors for category/event cards — cream (#e9e0b7), lavender (#eeeaef), sage (#b7d0e6), blush (#feedeb), warm gray (#b4af9c). The Knot uses white (#ffffff) exclusively.
palette.neutral_role: Peerspace body text #121212 (same as primary — very dark). Eventbrite body #39364f (warm dark gray-purple). The Knot body #37393f (medium gray). All three avoid pure #000 for body text.
palette.border_role: Peerspace uses #6a6e7a and #aeafbd for secondary text and borders. Eventbrite uses #c2c2cc. The Knot uses #cacce0. All muted grays — borders are understated in venue sites.

typography.note: Peerspace uses weight 400 for all headings — even at 160px. The Knot uses 700 for headings. Eventbrite uses 600-700. Most venue sites use custom brand fonts with web-font loading.
typography.heading_style: Venue sites mix two heading modes: (1) large decorative display headings at 88-160px with tight or zero letter-spacing used as section markers (Peerspace 'Why / Peerspace' at 160px), and (2) functional section headings at 24-56px. The Knot is more restrained at 34-48px. Eventbrite headings are compact at 18-24px.

content_max_width.note: Peerspace uses ps-container-md with 48px horizontal padding. Eventbrite and The Knot use full-width layouts with internal grid constraints.

card_padding.typical: 16px 12px (Eventbrite event card), 0px 32px (The Knot list items), 8px 16px (Peerspace buttons as card-like elements)

border_radius.buttons: 2px (Peerspace — sharp rectangles), 25px (The Knot — pills), 100px (Eventbrite — full pills)
border_radius.cards: 0-8px (Peerspace — sharp), 0px (The Knot — no radius on listing items), varied (Eventbrite event cards — sharp to 8px)

elevation.shadows: Minimal to none across all three brands. Peerspace uses rgba(0,0,0,0.05) 0px 16px 40px 4px on some elements. The Knot and Eventbrite use flat design with no card shadows — relying on borders and spacing for separation.
elevation.style: Flat design dominant. Event venue sites prioritize large photography over card elevation. Cards are often borderless with image-first layouts.

typical_order: header (sticky/fixed nav with logo, search trigger, locations dropdown, Sign Up / Log In)
hero (full-bleed venue photography, large display heading over image, prominent search bar with location + date + guest count, CTA 'Find your space' / 'Search')
category/activity grid (icon + label cards — Photo Shoot, Meeting, Party, Wedding, Workshop)
featured venues / top picks (image-heavy cards with name + location + capacity + price)
popular locations / cities grid (image tiles with city name overlay)
how it works (3-step: Search → Book → Enjoy — icon + short description)
trust/social proof (ratings, review counts, 'Best of' awards, host badges, press logos)
venue type taxonomy (House, Bar, Loft, Gallery, Warehouse — image + label)
inspiration / blog / ideas section (article cards with images)
host CTA (dark background section — 'Earn income as a host' with secondary CTA)
footer (dark background, 4-5 column link grid, social icons, copyright)
hero_variants: Full-bleed venue photo with overlay text + floating search bar (Peerspace: dark overlay on photo, white text, 88px heading, search bar below)
Search-first hero (Eventbrite: large search input with autocomplete as primary hero element, minimal heading text)
Directory/search header (The Knot: category-style hero with filtering sidebar, less dramatic photography, more utilitarian)
card_variants: Venue card: large photo (60-70% of card height) + venue name + location + capacity + price/hourly rate + rating stars + favorite/bookmark icon
Category card: icon in circle (50% border-radius) + category name centered below (Eventbrite: 80px icon circles)
Location tile: full-bleed city image + city name overlay text + venue count
Event/date card: date badge + event title + venue name + price from + category tag

tone_profile.headline_style: Short, declarative, emotionally evocative. Peerspace: 'Find a space. Fulfill your vision.' / 'Where extraordinary begins.' The Knot: 'Wedding Venues on The Knot' (more functional). Eventbrite: 'Browsing events in [City]' (contextual/personalized). Style: sentence case or title case, never ALL CAPS. Concise — typically 3-7 words.
tone_profile.cta_style: Action-oriented first person or imperative. Peerspace: 'Find your space', 'Browse all activities', 'Discover the possibilities'. The Knot: 'Search', 'Sign up', 'Log in'. Eventbrite: 'Find Events', 'Sign in', 'Find my tickets'. CTA copy avoids 'Submit' or 'Click here' — uses aspirational or benefit-oriented language. Buttons alternate between dark (#121212) and white (#ffffff) for contrast.
trust_signals: Star ratings and review counts on venue cards
Number of bookings or events hosted
Host profiles with photos and response rates
anti_patterns: Avoid stock photography that doesn't show real venues
Avoid dense text walls — venue pages are visual-first
Avoid generic CTAs like 'Submit' or 'Learn more'
Avoid cold/sterile color palettes (blues, grays) — warm tones preferred
Avoid complex navigation — search should be prominent and always accessible
Avoid hiding pricing — venue sites show prices upfront on cards

color_mood: Warm + editorial (Peerspace: near-black + cream + deep purple accents — gallery-like sophistication)
Romantic + soft (The Knot: hot pink accent + clean white + dark gray — wedding-focused warmth)
Vibrant + energetic (Eventbrite: warm multicolor backgrounds — mustard, lavender, sage, blush — festival/community energy)
typography_mood: Editorial minimal (Peerspace: custom sans at weight 400, very large display sizes, tight letter-spacing)
Friendly bold (The Knot: custom rounded sans at weight 700, pill buttons, approachable)
Modern geometric (Eventbrite: Neue Plak, 600-700 weight, pill buttons, compact)
layout_density: Photography-first sparse (Peerspace: minimal text, large images, generous whitespace — 140px section padding)
Grid-dense functional (The Knot: multi-column link grids, sidebar filters, tighter content density)
Card-feed balanced (Eventbrite: scrollable card feed, moderate density, image + details pattern)

ui_patterns_unique_to_venue.search_bar_prominence: Venue sites universally feature a prominent search bar — often in the hero or just below the nav. The search typically includes: location (city/zip), date picker, guest count / capacity selector, and venue type dropdown. It is the primary interaction point.
ui_patterns_unique_to_venue.date_picker: Present on Peerspace (date input detected). Critical for venue booking flow. Typically inline calendar or date range picker.
ui_patterns_unique_to_venue.capacity_display: Venue cards show capacity (e.g. 'Up to 50 guests') as a key decision factor alongside price.
ui_patterns_unique_to_venue.price_display: Hourly rate is standard ('$150/hr') rather than total price. Eventbrite shows 'from $X'. Peerspace shows hourly rates.
ui_patterns_unique_to_venue.photo_gallery: Venue detail pages universally feature masonry or carousel photo galleries. Card thumbnails are typically 4:3 or 16:9 aspect ratio.
ui_patterns_unique_to_venue.map_integration: Location is critical — many venue sites embed maps or show 'nearby' suggestions.
ui_patterns_unique_to_venue.favorite_save: Heart/bookmark icon on venue cards for saving to wishlists.
ui_patterns_unique_to_venue.inquiry_cta: Venue cards often have dual CTAs: 'Book now' (instant) and 'Message host' / 'Request pricing' (inquiry-based).
